source.original_title: 05/08/2026 - Varun Shankar & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/08/2026 - Varun Shankar & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: Leicester, UK (as stated on this call)

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: You spoke with Kim, I think, right? Yes, I did, yeah. Okay, cool. Yeah, he kind of gave me a little bit of a background.

prospect.name: Varun Shankar
prospect.training_background: Three years of competitive rowing — three water sessions and two ERG sessions a week, plus two circuit-based HIIT sessions — so a seven-session week until roughly ten months ago. Training collapsed after a house move and a job change with a longer commute, and losing access to rowing. Currently runs 30-40 minutes every other day and returned to a gym last week. Found the company through Trevor's Instagram and has tried one kettlebell movement.

signals: Lost ground to a hard season — house move, job change, longer commute, loss of access to rowing: 'I lost a lot of time, or I felt like I lost a lot of time'
Wants a former self back and names the benchmark: 'do as many push-ups as I was able to before'
Regret is explicit and self-directed: 'I was able to do this, but now I'm not, so a bit annoyed at myself'
Counter-signal: still runs every other day and is only ten months detrained, so the decline is shallow — he sits close to the optimizer boundary and is younger and fitter than a typical rebuilder

goals.text: Reduce body fat, without a specific weight target — 'I'm not too fussed about the weight'
Improve strength and conditioning, particularly shoulders and lats
Get back to being able to do a full pull-up and as many push-ups as before
Be able to engage and leverage his core again
Build strength while staying functional and not stiff
Feel more capable and not tired after exertion
Get back into a consistent rhythm of training

pains.text: Perceived loss of strength since detraining — 'I just am not able to push as much as I could'
Discouraged and annoyed at himself when comparing current capability to his rowing days
Time lost to a longer commute and a more demanding job
Lost access to rowing after moving, leaving him with no set training pattern
Mental barrier to getting back into a gym rhythm
Not keen on conventional gym weightlifting as a route back

objections.raw_quote: I think that's yeah it's quite helpful i I'll have a think, and then would I get back to you, or like...
objections.rep_response: Made no attempt to hold the conversation. Offered to send a link and disengaged: 'Yeah, I'll just text you the link over, and if you want to do it, do it. If you don't, don't. That's fine.'

tiers.billing: per month, rolling, no commitment period
tiers.name: Skool self-guided community

evidence: No payment taken, no link sent on the call, no next call booked, no date agreed
Prospect deferred: 'I'll have a think, and then would I get back to you, or like...'
Rep closed the loop with 'I'll send you the link over. If you want to do it, you can sign up on the link. If not, that's fine as well.'
Positive intent toward the low-tier product only: 'No, I think it's quite helpful. And I think, yeah, it's definitely the right kind of exercises that I was thinking of doing.'

Counter-evidence for reading this as lost: the one-to-one coaching was effectively abandoned by the rep, not refused by the prospect — the prospect was given a price fork and immediately answered 'Self-guided, please', and the coaching was never presented, defended or re-offered
Counter-evidence for reading this as follow_up: nothing was scheduled and the rep placed the entire onus on the prospect, so there is no follow-up mechanism beyond a text message
outcome.next_step: Rep to text a sign-up link for the £150/month Skool community. No call, date or commitment agreed.

notable.note: The rep offered an unapproved £150/month self-guided Skool tier alongside the coaching, asked the prospect to choose between them, and let him self-select the cheaper option with no discovery of budget and no attempt to sell the coaching. He also misstated the coaching's monthly equivalent as £880 when £4,400 over six months is £733 — a figure he stated correctly on another call the same day — which inflates the gap between the two products by roughly twenty per cent at the exact moment of choice. The call skipped the philosophy presentation, the consequence frame and the commitment check entirely, going from discovery to price in one step at the twelve-minute mark. No health, injury, age, weight or occupation question was asked at any point.

quality.notes: Frequent short-turn inversion. The rep's questions are repeatedly attached to the prospect's label and vice versa — 'What are you finding difficult about it? Because it's different for everybody' at 00:07:15 is split across both labels, and the long block from 00:16:56 to 00:18:07 runs the rep's product explanation and the prospect's questions together under alternating labels. Role was read from content throughout. The prospect's label is a first name only.
